records.Concise description: JAN3's mobile self-custody wallet combining on-chain Bitcoin and Liquid-based payment rails, including Lightning interoperability through swaps.
records.Deeper researched summary: AQUA is a mobile self-custody wallet for Bitcoin and Liquid assets. It emphasizes a unified payment experience across on-chain BTC, Liquid and Lightning-compatible payments while retaining local seed control. Lightning functionality is commonly implemented through swaps between Liquid and Lightning rather than by running a native Lightning node on the phone.
records.Launch / history: The current JAN3-led AQUA wallet generation developed through the 2020s and remained actively maintained in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: AQUA is important for showing a distinct wallet architecture: user-controlled Bitcoin and Liquid balances can interoperate with Lightning payments without requiring the user to manage Lightning channels directly.
Important technical or cultural characte: Self-custody; recovery seed controlled by user
Liquid asset / USDt support where available
Unified payment UX across multiple Bitcoin-related rails
records.Verification basis: Current official AQUA product/documentation material verifies self-custody, mobile platforms and Bitcoin/Liquid/Lightning payment architecture.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe AQUA as a native Lightning-node wallet; Lightning payments can be mediated by Liquid swap infrastructure.
Liquid trust/security assumptions differ from Bitcoin mainchain consensus and should be explained separately in public copy.

records.Concise description: Magic Eden's former multi-chain wallet, historically relevant to Bitcoin Ordinals and Runes but discontinued in 2026.
records.Deeper researched summary: Magic Eden Wallet offered browser/mobile access to multiple chains and was integrated with Magic Eden's Bitcoin marketplace and Runes/Ordinals ecosystem. Magic Eden ended Bitcoin marketplace support in March 2026, removed wallet support/downloads after April 1 and planned complete wallet shutdown for May 1. Its current Help Center treats the product as deprecated and directs users to export private keys and migrate.
records.Launch / history: Magic Eden launched its wallet during the 2020s multi-chain expansion. Bitcoin marketplace support ended March 9, 2026; Bitcoin/Runes APIs ended March 27; wallet support/downloads ended April 1, with full shutdown planned for May 1, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is a useful historical example of a marketplace-linked Bitcoin asset wallet and shows why software availability, service backends and company product status must be tracked separately.
Important technical or cultural characte: Ordinals / Runes / marketplace integration during active period
Wallet product and Bitcoin backend services discontinued in 2026
records.Verification basis: Current Magic Eden Help Center deprecation and service-shutdown documentation establishes INACTIVE status and migration requirements.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not present Magic Eden Wallet as currently supported even if an old installation still opens locally.
The wallet product and Magic Eden's surviving marketplace/business are separate lifecycle questions.
Migration guidance exposed private-key export; never instruct users to share exported keys.

records.Concise description: ACINQ's self-custody mobile Lightning wallet that automates channel and liquidity management while keeping user-controlled keys.
records.Deeper researched summary: Phoenix runs a Lightning wallet on the user's device and abstracts much of the channel-management complexity through ACINQ's Lightning infrastructure and automated liquidity mechanisms. It also supports on-chain Bitcoin interoperability from the same wallet. Current 2026 versions use modern Lightning features including splicing and Taproot-related channel evolution.
records.Launch / history: Phoenix launched in 2019 and has evolved through major Lightning architecture changes; version 2.8.x was current in mid-2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Phoenix is one of the most influential examples of making self-custodial Lightning usable without requiring users to manually operate a traditional server node.
Important technical or cultural characte: Automated channel/liquidity management through ACINQ services
records.Verification basis: Current ACINQ/Phoenix product and 2026 release material verify active mobile operation and current Lightning architecture.
Research notes / uncertainties: Self-custody of keys does not mean no dependency on ACINQ-operated services for liquidity/user experience.
Public copy should distinguish wallet-key custody from routing/LSP/service dependencies.

records.Entity / project type: mobile Bitcoin / Lightning wallet and node interface
records.Concise description: An open-source mobile Bitcoin and Lightning wallet that can connect to remote nodes or run an embedded Lightning node, with a 2026 graduated onboarding model.
records.Deeper researched summary: ZEUS began as a mobile controller for users' Lightning nodes and evolved into a wallet with embedded node options. Version 13 made LDK Node the default embedded backend for new self-custodial node users while retaining support for prior LND configurations and remote nodes. Its 'Mortal' onboarding also uses Cashu ecash before sweeping to self-custody, so the custody model depends on which mode and asset balance a user is actually using.
records.Launch / history: Shipping since 2019. Version 13.0.0 launched April 27, 2026 with the graduated-wallet design and LDK Node as the new default embedded engine.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: ZEUS is important because it spans three wallet roles—remote-node controller, embedded Lightning node and simple payment onboarding—without forcing advanced infrastructure on every user.
Important technical or cultural characte: Embedded LDK Node for new advanced/self-custodial path
Cashu ecash onboarding in Mortal mode
records.Verification basis: Current ZEUS wallet and v13 first-party material verify active operation and the new embedded-node/cashu architecture.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not label every ZEUS balance/path unqualified 'self-custodial': Cashu ecash has mint trust/custody characteristics even though ZEUS describes a path toward self-custodial Lightning.
Distinguish remote-node, embedded-node and ecash configurations in public copy.
